Halo3ODST.nameResolution:
HCM has NOTHING usable here: GetDebugString.cpp/.h is Halo2-only (its `stringIDDataFields`, `debugStringTableAddress` 0xE98AE0 and `debugStringMetaTableAddress` 0xE80AE0 VersionedEntries exist for Halo2 and no other game), and its source comment literally says "just doing the h2 impl for now" / "will have to see how h3+ handles it". ODST does not use Halo2's flat index+offset table at all.

The realistic path is to call the engine's own resolver: halo3odst.dll+0x1272C4, `char* __fastcall string_id_get_string(int string_id)`. It returns nullptr for an unknown id. Internals (if you would rather reimplement): it does `entry = hash_find(*(void**)(module+0x2029340), string_id)` using halo3odst.dll+0x1429D8, then `memcpy(&offset, entry+0x18, *(u64*)(table+0x08))` and returns `module+0x2DAA740 + offset`. Reimplementing is possible but unattractive — hash_find dispatches through two function pointers stored at table+0x10 (hash fn) and table+0x18 (compare fn), so you would be reimplementing a virtual hash table rather than indexing an array. Recommend the direct call; it is a read-only lookup with no engine state mutation.

Practical fallback that needs no string resolution at all: a zone set whose name string_id is 0 / unresolvable is the unnamed one; synthesise "(internal zone set N)" exactly as HCESwitchZoneSet.cpp already does, and — unlike HaloCER — you can still switch to it, because the ODST switch takes an INDEX, not a name (see switchMechanism). So the GUI does not need to filter unnamed entries out at all.

Halo3ODST.switchMechanism:
Option (a) is DEAD and option (c) is WRONG for this feature; the right answer is a variant of (b) — a two-word write to the engine's own pending-switch state, which is exactly what the HaloScript function itself does.

(a) `switch_zone_set` DOES exist as a HaloScript function in ODST (name string at 0x180815DD0, table entry 0x18082D098, impl 0x180225804), but HCM has NO script/console injection path for any MCC title. HCEConsole.cpp / HCEConsoleBridge / HCEScriptRegistry are all HCE-prefixed (Halo Campaign Evolved / HaloSimulation_tag_release.dll) and do not apply. CommandConsoleManager is HCM's own internal command console, not a game script console. So the HaloCER approach of queueing a text command cannot be ported.

(c) Writing `currentBSPSet` (halo3odst.dll+0x46E261C) the way SwitchBSPSet.cpp does changes only the loaded-BSP bitmask. It does NOT change the zone set: `dword_1808E0B94` stays put, the designer-zone masks stay stale, the PVS still comes from the old zone set's pvs index, and no zone-set-change notifications fire. Do not use it.

(b) RECOMMENDED — write the engine's pending-switch pair, in this order:
      *(int32_t*)(halo3odst.dll + 0x20FF6D0) = zoneSetIndex;   // pending zone set index
      *(uint8_t*)(halo3odst.dll + 0x20FF6C1) = 1;              // "a switch is pending" flag
    Index first, then flag, so the sim thread can never observe the flag set with a stale index.
    The engine's per-frame main update (sub_1800BF924) does `if (byte_1820FF6C1) sub_1800C1208();`, and sub_1800C1208 calls `sub_1800A8E60(dword_1820FF6D0)` (main_switch_structure_bsp) which performs the real switch and then clears both globals itself (writes index = -1, flag = 0). No cleanup needed from HCM.
    This is directly analogous in risk profile to what SwitchBSPSet.cpp already does today (a plain global write from HCM's thread, picked up by the sim thread next tick).

    Bounds: reject index < 0 or index >= *(int32_t*)(scenario + 0x74) before writing — the engine's own script impl does exactly this and there is no bounds check on the commit path.

Because the mechanism takes an INDEX, the HaloCER limitation "the internal zone set has no name so HaloScript cannot address it" does NOT apply to ODST. Every zone set, named or not, is switchable. GUIHCESwitchZoneSet's `switchable()` filter should be dropped for this game and all entries listed.
Halo3ODST.switchMechanismAlternatives:
Direct calls, if you would rather invoke engine code than write globals (both are __fastcall, both are the literal HaloScript implementations):
  halo3odst.dll+0xC0D9C  `void switch_zone_set(int index /*ecx*/, int64_t unused /*rdx*/)` — full script behaviour: bounds-checks against scenario+0x74, refuses if already on that zone set (prints "tried to switch to current zone-set %d"), otherwise sets the same two globals and tail-calls sub_1802FF07C(1). Pass rdx = 0; it is only consumed as a printf vararg on the error paths. Disassembly at 0x1800C0D9C confirms ecx is the index and is preserved into the sub_1800A8C34 call.
  halo3odst.dll+0xC0E20  `void prepare_to_switch_to_zone_set(int index, int64_t unused)` — sets dword at +0x20FF6CC and the byte at +0x20FF6C0 (HIBYTE of word_1820FF6BF); the main loop then calls sub_1800A8DB0. This is the "begin" half; it pre-loads without committing. Only needed if you want to mirror the begin/commit split.
  halo3odst.dll+0xA8E60  main_switch_structure_bsp(unsigned int zoneSetIndex) — the actual commit worker. DO NOT call this from HCM's thread: it dereferences `NtCurrentTeb()->ThreadLocalStoragePointer[TlsIndex]` to reach per-thread game state, so it is only valid on the engine's own thread. Same trap class as the CER sim-TLS trap. The global-write approach in switchMechanism exists precisely to avoid this.
  sub_1802FF07C (called by the script impl after setting the globals) also touches TLS. That is one more reason to prefer the plain global writes over calling 0xC0D9C: the global-write path runs entirely on the engine thread.

Not useful here: `switch_map_and_zone_set` (0x180124904, loads a different map), `current_zone_set_fully_active` (0x180225840).
Halo3ODST.currentZoneSetRead:
halo3odst.dll + 0x8E0B94, int32_t, -1 when no scenario/zone set is loaded. This is proven the strongest way available: the HaloScript function `current_zone_set` (name string 0x180815DE0, table entry 0x18082D058) has implementation sub_180225830 whose entire body is `return hs_return(a2, dword_1808E0B94);` — the global IS what the script returns. It is also the value sub_1800A8F08 writes on a successful commit, and the value every other site uses to index the zone set block (`block[10 * dword_1808E0B94 + N]`).

⚠ TRAP — DO NOT REUSE HCM's `currentBSP` FOR ODST. HCM's existing `currentBSP` VersionedEntry for Halo3ODST 1.3528 is halo3odst.dll+0x8E0B90, which is the ADJACENT global, four bytes low. For HaloReach (0xAFBE30) and Halo4 (0xE5BB50) HCM's `currentBSP` and `currentZoneSet` entries are byte-identical, which makes it very tempting to assume the same aliasing holds for ODST. It does not. 0x8E0B90 is the scenario/map load-state index (tested `== -1` for "no scenario loaded" by the script name resolvers, written at 0x1800B3B7B on scenario load, reset to -1 next to the zone set index in sub_1800A863C). Using it as the zone set index would be off-by-one-field and would silently produce a plausible wrong number.

Count/max sanity gate for the read, mirroring HCESwitchZoneSet::currentIndex: treat v < 0 or v > 0x30 as "unknown".

Halo3ODST.portNotes:
Differences the C++ port must handle versus HCESwitchZoneSet.cpp:

1. Tag access model. HaloCER walks a tag address table and decodes a packed tag handle (`regionBase + 4*encoded`). ODST does none of that: HCM's existing scenario-tag-address service plus TagBlockReader (already wired for Halo3ODST — GetTriggerData uses both) cover it. Drop resolveTagBlock() entirely.

2. Names. char[256] literal -> u32 string_id. The whole `buffer[257]` / printable-character scan in refresh() goes away and is replaced by a string_id resolve. Budget real work for this: HCM has no string_id resolver for any H3-era title (GetDebugString is Halo2-only).

3. The switch is by INDEX, not by name. This is a simplification: delete the "that zone set has no name in the tag, so HaloScript cannot address it" rejection in switchTo(), and delete GUIHCESwitchZoneSet::switchable() / the whole engineIndex-vs-row mapping. Every row is switchable and row order == engine order. The "(internal zone set N)" placeholder label is still worth keeping for display.

4. Constants that change: kZoneSetBlock 0xD0 -> 0x74, kZoneSetStride 0x130 -> 0x28, kZoneSetNameOffset 0x004(char[256]) -> 0x00(string_id), kZoneSetFlagsOffset 0x108 -> 0x08 (bit values unchanged: 0x4 == internal), kMaxZoneSets 64 -> 48.

5. No signature scanning. HaloCER needs byte signatures because it has no version resource; halo3odst.dll is versioned (1.3528.0.0) and HCM already keys everything off that, so these go in InternalPointerData.xml as plain module offsets like every other MCC entry.

6. Threading. The HCEConsoleBridge queue-onto-sim-thread machinery has no MCC equivalent and is not needed: the recommended mechanism is two plain global writes that the sim thread consumes on its next tick, same shape as SwitchBSPSet.cpp. Do NOT be tempted to call sub_1800A8E60 (+0xA8E60) directly — it reads game state through NtCurrentTeb()->ThreadLocalStoragePointer and is only valid on the engine thread.

7. Invalidate-on-level-change still applies verbatim (the scenario pointer moves), and reading currentZoneSet is a single u32 module-offset read, so GetCurrentZoneSet.cpp works unmodified once the XML entry exists — it currently throws for Halo3ODST purely because the VersionedEntry is absent.

8. ODST firefight: I found no firefight-specific divergence. The zone set system, block offset, stride and globals are scenario-wide and not campaign-only, and there is no second code path keyed on game mode anywhere in the readers I walked. I did NOT confirm this by inspecting a firefight scenario's actual zone set contents (that needs a cache-map parse I did not do), so treat "firefight behaves identically" as untested rather than proven.

HaloReach.switchMechanism:
Write the engine's own pending-switch request globals, then let the game thread commit. Two writes, order matters:
  1) int32 at haloreach.dll+0x263EAD4 = target zone set index
  2) uint8 at haloreach.dll+0x263EAC2 = 1
Validate 0 <= index < scenario[0xAC] YOURSELF first; the pump does not re-validate (only the script impl does).
Consumption path, all on the game thread: sub_180033A88 (+0x33A88, the main-loop pending-action pump) tests the byte at +0x263EAC2 and calls sub_180035608 (+0x35608), which does sub_180015034(dword at +0x263EAD4), then clears index to -1 and the flag to 0. sub_180015034 -> sub_1800150D4 (+0x150D4) -> sub_180014E40 (+0x14E40), which is exactly the function HCM already hooks at ZoneSetChangeFunction haloreach.dll+0x14E7B, so the existing ZoneSetChangeHookEvent will fire for switches HCM initiates.
This is the same already-shipping pattern HCM uses for HaloReach forceCheckpointFlag (+0x263EABE) and forceRevertFlag (+0x263EABB): those live in the SAME flag block (0x263EAB8..0x263EAD8) pumped by the same sub_180033A88. No thread affinity required for the writes.
A "prepare to switch" variant also exists: int32 at +0x263EAD0 plus uint8 at +0x263EAC1, consumed by sub_180014EB0 (+0x14EB0).

HaloReach.portNotes:
1. The switch is a two-word global write, not a call. Write the index first, then the flag, or the pump can commit a stale index. Validate the index against scenario[0xAC] yourself.
2. Do NOT call sub_180035370 / sub_180015034 / sub_180014EB0 from an HCM thread. All three reach TLS via NtCurrentTeb()->ThreadLocalStoragePointer[TlsIndex].
3. No HaloScript route. HCEConsoleBridge does not exist for MCC titles, so the HaloCER design (format a "switch_zone_set NAME" string and queue it) must be replaced by index-based dispatch. Consequence: HCM can address unnamed zone sets in Reach, unlike HaloCER. The GUIHCESwitchZoneSet filter that hides names beginning with "(" should be dropped for Reach, and the engine-index vs row-index remapping becomes unnecessary.
4. Name reading is identical to HaloCER: literal char[256], just at a different element offset base and a different stride. Do not build a string_id resolver.
5. Reuse HCM's existing services rather than the HaloCER signature scan: GetScenarioAddress (haloreach.dll+0xC1A230) plus TagBlockReader (count at +0, encoded address at +4) already decode the block. HCESwitchZoneSet.cpp's private resolveTagBlock/resolveAnchors and its HCESignatureScan dependency have no place in the MCC port.
6. Free win: because the commit path runs through sub_180014E40, the existing ZoneSetChangeHookEvent (hook at +0x14E7B) fires on HCM-initiated switches, so the GUI "current" marker updates itself with no extra polling.
7. The overlay features that read zone sets should read +0x114 for "which BSPs does this zone set pull in", not +0x10C.
8. A separate debug global disable_switch_zone_sets exists in Reach's config table (name string +0x9F2FD0). Not investigated; if a switch silently no-ops, check it.

Halo4.switchMechanism:
WRITE TWO GLOBALS AND LET THE ENGINE'S OWN PER-TICK PUMP COMMIT IT. This is option (b)-lite and is the same shape SwitchBSPSet.cpp / ForceCheckpoint already use.

  1. write int32  at halo4.dll+0x293DEC8 = target zone set index
  2. write uint8  at halo4.dll+0x293DEB4 = 1

On the next game tick the deferred-action pump sub_1800607C8 (halo4.dll+0x607C8) executes `if (byte_18293DEB4) sub_1800626F8();`. sub_1800626F8 (halo4.dll+0x626F8) then calls sub_180045738(dword_18293DEC8) — the real zone-set switch — and afterwards clears BOTH globals itself (dword_18293DEC8 = -1; byte_18293DEB4 = 0). So HCM writes and forgets; no unhook, no cleanup, no thread marshalling.

Why this is safe and not a guess: the exact same flag block is ALREADY used by shipping HCM features on this exact module and version. InternalPointerData.xml has forceCheckpointFlag = halo4.dll+0x293DEAF, forceRevertFlag = halo4.dll+0x293DEAB, forceMissionRestartFlag = halo4.dll+0x293DE28 — and sub_1800607C8 is literally the function that tests word_18293DEAF ("checkpoint save") and the rest of that byte block. Zone set switching is byte_18293DEB4 in the same struct, checked in the same function, two lines away.

HCM must do the validation that sub_18006252C would have done, because writing the flag bypasses it:
  - index >= 0 and index < *(int32*)(scenarioAddress + 0x100)
  - index != *(int32*)(halo4.dll + 0xE5BB50)  (switching to the current set is a no-op the engine logs as an error)
An out-of-range index would make sub_180045738 index off the end of the zone set block, so this check is mandatory, not cosmetic.

There is also a "prepare to switch" (async preload, does not commit) if wanted later: int32 at halo4.dll+0x293DEC4 = index, uint8 at halo4.dll+0x293DEB3 = 1, pumped by the adjacent `if (HIBYTE(word_18293DEB2)) sub_1800626A0();`.
Halo4.switchMechanismAlternatives:
(a) HaloScript 'switch_zone_set' — EXISTS as a script function but is NOT a realistic path. The string "switch_zone_set" is at 0x180D08DC0 and is registered at 0x18015978D inside sub_1801466E4 with description "switches to a different zone set" and implementation pointer sub_18006252C (halo4.dll+0x6252C). 'prepare_to_switch_to_zone_set' -> sub_1800625B8 (halo4.dll+0x625B8). BUT: HCM has no console / script-injection path for any MCC title. Grepping HCMInternal for ConsoleBridge/hs_command/script-inject hits only HCEConsole.cpp/.h, GUIHCEConsole.h, HCESwitchZoneSet.cpp and other HCE* files — every one of them HaloCER-only. Building an MCC script console is a whole separate project.

(b-direct) Directly calling sub_18006252C (halo4.dll+0x6252C, `void __fastcall(int index)`; the second hexrays arg is only the printf varargs passthrough for the error strings) — NOT RECOMMENDED. It is only a thin validator around exactly the two global writes recommended above, and it ends in sub_1803BF270, which dereferences `NtCurrentTeb()->ThreadLocalStoragePointer[TlsIndex]` to reach sim-thread state. Calling that from an HCM thread reads the wrong TLS slot. Writing the globals gets the same effect with the engine doing the call on its own thread.

(c) Writing the BSP mask the way SwitchBSPSet.cpp writes currentBSPSet (halo4.dll+0x4967A18) — DOES NOT WORK as a zone set switch. It loads/unloads BSPs only. It leaves currentZoneSet (halo4.dll+0xE5BB50) stale, and leaves the designer-zone mask (halo4.dll+0x275D5D0), cinematic-zone mask (halo4.dll+0x4967A64) and structure-design mask untouched, so the game would be on BSPs from one zone set with the designer/cinematic/design-zone state of another. Useful as a complement (HCM already ships it), not as the feature.

Verdict: implement (b)-lite (the two global writes). It is 6 lines and reuses an already-proven HCM mechanism.

Halo4.portNotes:
Differences from the HaloCER implementation the C++ port must handle:

1. ANCHORING. HaloCER byte-signature-scans because it has no version resource. Halo4 does NOT need that — use HCM's normal PointerDataStore / InternalPointerData.xml module-offset path, and use the existing GetScenarioAddress + TagBlockReader + StrideableDynamicStruct services instead of HCESwitchZoneSet.cpp's hand-rolled resolveTagBlock()/readPtr(). The tag-block encoding (tagAddressTable[enc>>28] + 4*enc) is already implemented inside TagBlockReaderImplMagic; do not reimplement it.

2. BLOCK OFFSET AND STRIDE. 0xD0 -> 0x100, 0x130 -> 0x1A0. Everything else about the reader is identical.

3. NAME. Offset moves 0x004 -> 0x004 (unchanged!) and it is still a literal char[256]. The name-reading loop in HCESwitchZoneSet.cpp::refresh() can be copied verbatim. Do NOT reach for GetDebugString — it is Halo2-only and there is no Halo4 string table entry in the XML.

4. FLAGS. 0x108 -> 0x108 (unchanged), but the bit meanings extend: Halo4 adds 0x8 'disable sky clearing' and 0x10 'override sky clear color'. Bit 0x4 is still 'internal zone set'. Note 0x10 is set on most shipped zone sets, so do NOT treat a non-zero flags word as "special".

5. THE GUI FILTER MUST CHANGE. GUIHCESwitchZoneSet filters out every zone set whose name is empty or starts with '(' because HaloCER switches BY NAME through HaloScript and cannot address the unnamed internal set. Halo4 switches BY INDEX through a global write, so NOTHING needs filtering — every zone set is switchable, and in practice every Halo 4 zone set has a real name anyway. Drop the switchable()/Entry{engineIndex,name} indirection for the Halo4 element, or keep the struct but never filter. Keeping the filter would be harmless today but is dead complexity.

6. THE SWITCH ITSELF. Replace `HCEConsoleBridge::queue(std::format("switch_zone_set {}", name), outWhy)` with two MultilevelPointer writes (index to halo4.dll+0x293DEC8, then uint8 1 to halo4.dll+0x293DEB4). verdicts.field: scenarioZoneSetTagBlock = 0xAC (count int32 @+0xAC, encoded block address uint32 @+0xB0)
verdicts.claimed: 0xAC. Count int32 at scenario+0xAC, encoded block address uint32 at scenario+0xB0. HCM hypothesis CONFIRMED.
verdicts.howIChecked: Cache-map structural walk, no disassembly used. Built a Reach MCC cache parser in Python: located the special-tag list ('ward'/'xipg'/'yalp'/'!hgu'/'enoz'/'rncs'/'gtam' 8-byte entries), read the scnr datum handle (index 8, salt 0xE17E), then read the tag instance table entry {u16 groupIndex, u16 salt, u32 encAddress}. That gives the scenario tag's encoded address A WITHOUT knowing the file->address constant K. Then, for the zone-set element block located physically by its name chain at offset B, I scanned the ENTIRE file for every (count, enc) dword pair and computed the implied field offset = p - B + 4*(enc - A), which is K-free. In m10.map that returned EXACTLY ONE hit in 421 MB, at field offset 0xAC. Repeated on m20/m30/m35/m45/m50/m52/m60/m70: all nine maps returned 0xAC, and the implied K came out page-aligned (multiple of 0x1000) in every case, while the only spurious hits (m52, offsets 0x5A8/0x5C0) produced a non-page-aligned K. Campaign: m10=10, m20=8, m30=8, m35=11, m45=18, m50=7, m52=7, m60=13, m70=13. campaign.map and shared.map carry no scnr at all.

verdicts.field: portNote 3: drop the "(" name filter and the engine-index/row-index remapping for Reach
verdicts.claimed: HCM can address unnamed zone sets in Reach, unlike HaloCER; drop the filter.
verdicts.howIChecked: Agreed, and the reason is stronger than they state: across all 130 shipped Reach zone-set elements, ZERO have an empty name at +0x04 and ZERO have flags bit 2 (internal) set. So the HaloCER '(internal zone set N)' synthesiser and the GUIHCESwitchZoneSet 'name.front() != (' filter are dead code for Reach, not merely unnecessary. Keep a defensive fallback for a corrupt read, but it will never fire on retail data.

verdicts.field: Unknown #3: whether the debug global behind 'disable_switch_zone_sets' can block a queued switch
verdicts.claimed: Not traced; if a switch silently no-ops, check it.
verdicts.howIChecked: Partially closed. I disassembled the full producer (sub_180035370) and the full consumer (sub_180035608, 0x35608-0x3565F) and decompiled the pump body: none of them tests any config/debug global on the path from byte_18263EAC2 to sub_180015034 (the only other byte tested is byte_18263EBF8, which only selects whether a lock object is released). So a disable flag cannot block a switch that is already queued through these two globals. I did not trace what the string at 0x9F2FD0 is actually wired to, so I cannot say it has no effect at all elsewhere.

missedEntirely: The engine's switch_zone_set makes a THIRD call HCM's two-write path will skip: sub_180035370 tail-calls sub_1802C4610(1) after arming (and sub_180035608 calls sub_1802C4610(0) after committing). sub_1802C4610 reads NtCurrentTeb()->ThreadLocalStoragePointer[TlsIndex] and, when *(x+16)==1, loops calling sub_1802C4484(i, (a1^1)+712, 3) - it toggles some per-entity state 712/713. HCM cannot make that call (TLS), so an HCM-initiated switch will deliver only the 'off' half (0) via the pump, never the 'on' half (1). Probably benign, entirely untested, and the single biggest residual risk in the recommended design. Worth logging as a known deviation in the port.

The gate on the pump. The whole body of sub_180033A88 is wrapped in 'if (sub_1800356AC())'. Their write-the-globals plan only works because sub_1800356AC ORs in 'word_18263EAC1', a 16-bit read that covers byte 0x263EAC2. They never verified this link; if it had not been there, setting the byte would have been inert. Anyone re-deriving this for another MCC title must check the equivalent gate.

Write ORDER: the engine itself writes the FLAG first (0x1800353D6) and the INDEX second (0x1800353DF) - the opposite of what they recommend. Their recommendation (index first) is the correct one for a cross-thread writer, but their report presents it as if it mirrored the engine, which it does not.

The already-active guard. sub_180035370 calls sub_180014BB8(index) and either errors ('tried to switch to current zone-set %d') or CANCELS a pending switch. A raw two-global write bypasses that entirely, so writing index == currentZoneSet re-runs the full commit for the zone set you are already on rather than being rejected. Decide deliberately whether HCM should replicate the guard (it can: compare against currentZoneSet at 0xAFBE30).

The engine's tag-block decode is regionTable[enc>>28] + 4*enc, with the table at qword_184E39F20 - NOT the single-region 'magicAddress + tagBase 0x50000000 + (enc<<2)' that HCM's TagBlockReader uses for Reach. Every enc in every shipped Reach map has top nibble 5, so HCM's reader happens to be correct, but the port should know it is relying on that.

The name getter uses a DIFFERENT scenario handle. sub_180014B50 resolves through qword_180C1A600 + 8*(u16)dword_180AFBE38 + 4, not qword_180C1A230. The switch implementation validates against qword_180C1A230. For HCM, read names and count from GetScenarioAddress (0xC1A230) so the list and the index you submit come from the same struct.

cex_ff_halo.map - the one shipped map where element+0x10C != element+0x114. They sampled only six campaign maps and concluded the two were always equal; the counterexample is the whole justification for their own 'read 0x114' recommendation.

The complete shipped census. All 44 Reach maps, 130 elements: count is never 0, max is 18 (m45), no empty names, no flags bit 2, hint-previous is 0xFFFFFFFF in 130/130, audibility index is strictly sequential 0..N-1 in 130/130. Those last two are excellent cheap sanity checks for the runtime reader to assert on.

HCM already has most of the plumbing they propose to build: GetScenarioAddress, GetCurrentZoneSet (reads the 0xAFBE30 entry), ZoneSetChangeHookEvent (already subscribed by GetSoftCeilingData), TagBlockReader, and StrideableDynamicStruct. GetActiveStructureDesignTags.cpp ALREADY reads scenarioTagDataFields::ZoneSetTagBlock + zoneSetMetaDataFields at stride 0x13C for HaloReach in shipping code - which is independent operational evidence that 0xAC and 0x13C work at runtime, and which their report never mentions.

No dynamic verification of any kind was possible or done (anti-cheat), by them or by me. Nothing here proves the game actually performs the switch; it proves the data path exists and is reachable. The first real test should be: set index, set flag, then watch dword_180AFBE30 change and ZoneSetChangeHookEvent fire.
HaloReach.overallReadiness:
READY TO IMPLEMENT on the data side; the switch side is ready but carries one named, untested deviation.

Every offset they report is now confirmed by at least two genuinely independent paths, and two of their own caveats are closed: the trailing field at 0x130 IS a tag_block (runtime read site found, so the element provably closes at 0x13C), and the MP/Firefight question is answered (every shipped Reach map has at least one zone set; MP/FF/Forge have exactly one). Final values for the port, all verified: ZoneSetTagBlock 0xAC (count) / 0xB0 (encoded address); stride 0x13C; name = literal char[256] at element+0x04 with a string_id at +0x00 that HCM cannot resolve (GetDebugString is Halo2-only); pvs index 0x104; flags 0x108; authored bsp mask 0x10C; authored structure-design mask 0x110; RUNTIME bsp mask 0x114 (use this one - cex_ff_halo.map proves 0x10C is wrong there); runtime structure-design mask 0x118; required/forbidden designer zones 0x11C/0x120; cinematic zones 0x124; hint previous 0x128; audibility index 0x12C; tag_block 0x130..0x13B. currentZoneSet 0xAFBE30, ZoneSetChangeFunction 0x14E7B, scenarioAddress 0xC1A230, StructureBSPsTagBlock 0x50 all confirmed. Max 48 remains single-source (editing kit) and should be treated as a UI clamp only.

Three corrections to fold into the port: (1) their claim that 0x10C == 0x114 in all shipped caches is false - cex_ff_halo.map diverges, which is precisely why 0x114 must be the one read; (2) their claim that flags==1 marks exactly the terminal zone set is false (m20, m35, m50, m60, m70 contradict it, and m35 sets it on two elements) - harmless, but it means that particular cross-check was not really performed; (3) their claim that sub_180035370 does nothing beyond the two global writes is false - it also tail-calls sub_1802C4610(1), a TLS-dependent call HCM cannot make.

Remaining blockers: none for reading. For switching, one open risk to accept deliberately and log: the skipped sub_1802C4610(1) arm-side call, whose effect is unknown and cannot be tested statically. Ship the switch with the index validated against scenario[0xAC] by HCM itself (the pump does not re-validate and an out-of-range index is an unchecked OOB read), index written before flag, and preferably an explicit 'already on this zone set' rejection to reproduce the sub_180014BB8 guard the direct write bypasses. First live test should confirm dword_180AFBE30 changes and the existing ZoneSetChangeHookEvent fires.

verdicts.field: scenarioZoneSetTagBlock = 0x74 (entryCount at +0x74, u32 offset at +0x78, blockDefinition at +0x7C)
verdicts.howIChecked: Independent path: full static parse of the real MCC cache map halo3odst/maps/h100.map in Python (they used the DLL and sapien.exe; they explicitly did NOT parse a map). I located the cache tag table at file 0x121CF080 (entries {u16 groupIdx, u16 salt, u32 addr/4}) by finding the tag-groups table at 0x121FA028 and validating that tag index 8 has groupIdx 0x8A == 'scnr' and salt 0xE17E, matching the global-tags table handle 0xE17E0008; only one 'scnr' tag exists in the map. I then located the scenario tag data at file 0x1372DCEC by solving a single linear equation anchored on an independently-found structure-BSP reference block (the unique run of 11 'psbs' tag references at stride 0x6C at file 0x13463148) - the solution is unique across the whole 415MB file, and the implied partition base (0x13463000) is page-aligned and matches the partition-5 offset predicted from the tag table, a check I did not build in. At that scenario address: +0x18 count = 11 = exactly the 11 sbsp tags in the map; +0x74 count = 25; +0x78 -> a block that resolves to 25 real zone sets; +0x268 count = 3 (HCM's soft ceilings); +0x28C count = 179 whose block start is bit-exact with the trigger-volume block I found separately via orthonormal forward/up frames using HCM's shipped stride 0x7C. blockDefinition at +0x7C reads 0 for every block, consistent with HCM's 12-byte tagBlock struct. Repeated end-to-end on l300.map (8 BSPs, 10 zone sets) and sc100.map (4 BSPs, 5 zone sets): +0x74/+0x78 holds every time.

verdicts.field: How the runtime resolves the block address ('moduleBase + *(u32*)(scenario+0x78)')
verdicts.claimed: moduleBase + *(u32*)(scenario+0x78)
verdicts.howIChecked: Raw capstone disassembly of the accessors from the DLL file (no IDA/Hex-Rays), plus HCM's own shipped source. halo3odst.dll+0x19B010 does: rax = *(void**)(module+0x2022AA8); ecx = *(u32*)(scenario+0x78); rdx = rax + ecx*4; edx = *(u32*)(rdx + 5*idx*8 + 0xC). The base is the magic pointer global, NOT the module base, and the stored offset is SCALED BY 4. HCM's InternalPointerData.xml already ships magicAddress Halo3ODST = halo3odst.dll+0x2022AA8 and TagBlockReader.cpp already applies `in << 2` with tagBase 0 for Halo3ODST, so their bottom-line advice (reuse TagBlockReader verbatim) is right - but anyone implementing from their prose would compute a garbage address.
verdicts.corrected: blockAddress = *(void**)(halo3odst.dll + 0x2022AA8) + 4 * (*(u32*)(scenario + 0x78)); offset 0 means null block. This is exactly HCM's TagBlockReaderImplMagic<Halo3ODST> (magicAddress 0x2022AA8, tagBase 0, offsetTransformation in<<2).

verdicts.field: zoneSetStride = 0x28 (40 bytes)
verdicts.howIChecked: Proved by WALKING real data, not by quoting a struct size. In h100.map I walked all 25 elements at stride 0x28 from the block address computed from the tag block field: every element has flags<=7, a BSP mask whose set bits all fall below the scenario's BSP count (11), pad bytes at +0x26 zero, hint index -1, and audibility index exactly 0,1,2,...,24. Element 24 parses cleanly and the bytes immediately after it start a different, unrelated 12-byte-stride array (designer zones: {string_id, 1}, {string_id, 2}, {string_id, 4}, {string_id, 8}...), so the array ends exactly at 25*0x28. Decisive independent corroboration: the 25 name ids are 25 consecutive values (0x658..0x670) and resolve, with one constant table shift, to exactly 25 consecutive strings in the map's string blob - 'set_l100','set_050_cin','set_090_cin','set_040_cin','set_oni_cin','set_030_cin','set_000_cin','set_000','set_000_030','set_030','set_030_040','set_040','set_040_060','set_040_100','set_050','set_050_080','set_060_080','set_060_100','set_080_090','set_090','set_100_oni','set_oni','set_shaft','set_survival_a','set_survival_b' - in the same order. A wrong stride cannot produce a 25-for-25 ordered match. Also independently visible in raw disassembly as `lea rcx,[r8+r8*4]; mov edx,[rdx+rcx*8+0xC]` (5*8 = 40).

verdicts.field: name field: u32 string_id at element+0x00 (NOT a char array)
verdicts.claimed: string_id_u32 at +0x00
verdicts.howIChecked: Real cache data, per the task's explicit requirement to prove a real name resolves. h100.map's 25 zone set elements carry 0x658..0x670 at +0x00 - numeric, consecutive, no ASCII anywhere in the 40-byte element. Applying a single constant offset to the map's own string_id table (offset table at file 0x4000, 40639 entries; blob base 0x2C000, calibrated with 399/400 well-formed strings and a positive control strs[1]=='default', strs[10]=='melee') yields the 25 zone-set names listed above, in block order. The same constant applied to the independently-located trigger-volume block resolves its ids to 'begin_zone_set:set_000_030:*', 'zone_set:set_000_030:*', 'begin_zone_set:set_030_040:*'... - i.e. two different blocks in the same map both resolving to correct, thematically exact names. l300.map and sc100.map also carry numeric ids at +0x00 starting at 0x658. So: definitely a 4-byte id, definitely not char[].

verdicts.field: nameResolution: 'call halo3odst.dll+0x1272C4, string_id_get_string(int) -> char*, returns nullptr for an unknown id; read-only, no engine state mutation'
verdicts.claimed: safe read-only call, returns nullptr on failure
verdicts.howIChecked: Raw capstone disassembly of 0x1801272C4 and of the hash_find at 0x1801429D8 (they described the resolver from decompilation but did not check its failure modes). 0x1272C4 loads rdi = *(void**)(module+0x2029340) and calls hash_find(rdi, sext(id)) with NO null check. hash_find's first instruction on the table is `mov rax,[rcx+0x10]` (an indirect hash-fn pointer) followed by `div dword ptr [rsi]` (bucket count at table+0). So if the table pointer is null - which they themselves noted happens, it is zeroed at 0x1800B3CA5 / 0x18074C853 during load - the call ACCESS-VIOLATES rather than returning nullptr, and a zero bucket count divides by zero. Their 'returns nullptr for an unknown id' is true only for a populated table (the nullptr comes from the entry's offset == -1 path at 0x1802FE/0x180127303).
verdicts.corrected: The resolver is real and its mechanism is as described (hash_find -> entry+0x18 -> offset -> module+0x2DAA740 + offset), but it is NOT safe to call unguarded. The port must verify *(void**)(halo3odst.dll+0x2029340) != nullptr AND *(u32*)thatTable != 0 before calling, and must not call it when no map is loaded. Whether the call is safe from HCM's own thread remains UNPROVEN (it dispatches through two function pointers inside engine state).

verdicts.field: HCM has no usable string_id resolver (GetDebugString is Halo2-only)
verdicts.claimed: Halo2-only
verdicts.howIChecked: Read GetDebugString.cpp and grepped every Version node of its three dependencies in InternalPointerData.xml. debugStringTableAddress (line 10473), debugStringMetaTableAddress (10494) and stringIDDataFields (16105) each carry Halo2 versions only; the source comment is literally '// just doing the h2 impl for now'. Independent nuance they missed: HCM DOES already have HaloScriptOutputHookEvent with a Halo3ODST implementation (HaloScriptOutputHookEvent.cpp:377), so HCM already hooks ODST's HaloScript print path - it is output-only, not execution, but it is the one existing ODST script-system foothold.

verdicts.field: bsp zone flags at element+0x0C; runtime/'loaded' mask is the module global halo3odst.dll+0x46E261C (HCM's currentBSPSet); no second per-element runtime mask
verdicts.claimed: tag mask +0x0C, runtime mask module+0x46E261C
verdicts.howIChecked: Two paths neither of which is their cited one. (a) Raw disassembly of sub_1800A8C34 (which they never dumped): it returns true only if ecx == dword[0x8E0B94] AND (dword[0x46E261C] & sub_19B010(idx)) == sub_19B010(idx) AND (dword[0x46E2614] & sub_19B040(idx)) == sub_19B040(idx); sub_19B010 is byte-for-byte `zoneSetBlock[5*idx*8 + 0xC]`. That ties element+0x0C directly to the loaded-BSP global. Raw disassembly of sub_1800A8F08 confirms the commit writes dword[0x46E261C] = the mask argument (0x1800A9035), and dword[0x46E2618/2614/2610/260C] alongside; on failure it writes 0x8E0B94 = -1 and 0x46E261C = 0. sub_1800A863C resets 0x8E0B90, 0x8E0B94, 0x46E261C and the scenario pointer together. (b) Real cache data: every h100 bsp mask (0x108,0x140,0x104,0x380,0x400...) has all set bits below 11, the map's actual BSP count. 'No second per-element runtime mask' is confirmed by exhaustion - all ten dwords of the 0x28 element are accounted for by observed data.

verdicts.field: Full element layout: +0x04 pvs index, +0x08 flags, +0x10 required designer zones, +0x14 forbidden designer zones, +0x18 cinematic zones, +0x1C hint previous zone set, +0x20 audibility index, +0x24 short + 2 pad
verdicts.claimed: as listed, summing to 0x28
verdicts.howIChecked: Real h100 cache data, field by field, against structures I located independently. +0x04 takes values 0..15 and the scenario+0x5C 'zone set pvs' block has exactly 16 entries - the index is in range by construction. +0x10 and +0x14 are exact complements within 27 bits for every element (e.g. 0x078000D0 | 0x007FFF2F == 0x07FFFFFF), which is what required/forbidden designer-zone masks must look like. +0x18 holds sparse bitmasks (0x2003, 0x400C, 0x8030, 0x100C0, 0xA0300, 0x140C00) distinct from the BSP masks - consistent with their 'cinematic zones, not a second BSP mask' warning, though I did not independently prove the word 'cinematic'. +0x1C is -1 on all 25. +0x20 is exactly 0,1,2,...,24. +0x24 is 0xFFFF with the upper two bytes zero. The three flag names and their order are independently confirmed from the H3ODSTEK tag FILE h100.scenario's own embedded metadata blob (a different artifact from the sapien.exe definition tables they read): '...zone sets | pvs index | long block index | long flags | begin loading next level | debug purposes only | interal zone set | scenario_zone_set_flags_definition | bsp zone flags | required designer zones...'.

verdicts.field: flags at +0x08, bit2 (0x4) = internal zone set; port keeps the '(internal zone set N)' placeholder
verdicts.claimed: bit0 begin loading next level, bit1 debug only, bit2 internal
verdicts.howIChecked: Flag names and order from the EK tag file's own string blob (see above) - independent of sapien.exe. Field offset +0x08 forced by the confirmed neighbours (+0x04 pvs proven by the 16-entry pvs block, +0x0C proven by the runtime accessor). Real-data caveat they could not have seen: across h100 (25 zone sets), l300 (10) and sc100 (5), NOT ONE zone set has bit2 set, and every zone set has a non-zero name. Bit0 ('begin loading next level') IS used - l300 elements 5 and 9, sc100 element 3. So HaloCER's assumption that every level ships an unnamed internal zone set does not hold in ODST; the '(internal zone set N)' placeholder path is effectively dead code here, while switching INTO a bit0 zone set can plausibly kick off a level transition - a user-facing hazard nobody flagged.

verdicts.field: switchMechanism: write *(i32*)(module+0x20FF6D0) = index, then *(u8*)(module+0x20FF6C1) = 1; main loop consumes and self-clears
verdicts.claimed: two global writes consumed by sub_1800BF924 -> sub_1800C1208 -> sub_1800A8E60, which clears index=-1 and flag=0
verdicts.howIChecked: Method-independent: byte-level xref scan (I scanned all 7.6MB of .text for RIP displacements resolving to each target and re-decoded each candidate instruction with capstone) plus linear disassembly bounded by the .pdata RUNTIME_FUNCTION table - no IDA, no Hex-Rays. Every xref to both globals is accounted for. 0x1800BFA89: `mov al,[rip->0x20FF6C1]; test al,al; je +5; call 0x1800C1208`. 0x1800C1208: `mov ecx,[rip->0x20FF6D0]; call 0x1800A8E60` then `or dword[rip->0x20FF6D0], 0xFFFFFFFF; mov byte[rip->0x20FF6C1], 0`, with the error string 'main_switch_structure_bsp() failed' on the failure path confirming the callee's identity. The script impl at 0x1800C0D9C sets exactly these two globals (flag=1 at 0x1800C0DFF, index at 0x1800C0DEF). Their index-then-flag ordering is safer than the engine's own (the engine sets flag first).

verdicts.field: Bounds check required before writing (reject index<0 or >= *(i32*)(scenario+0x74))
verdicts.claimed: no bounds check on the commit path
verdicts.howIChecked: Raw disassembly of the commit chain: sub_1800C1208 passes dword[0x20FF6D0] straight into sub_1800A8E60 with no validation, and the only guard downstream is sub_19B010's `cmp r8d,-1`. An out-of-range index therefore reads zoneSetBlock[40*idx] out of bounds. The script path's own guard is visible at 0x1800C0DC5 (`cmp ebx,[rax+0x74]; jge error`) and at 0x1800C0E3C for the prepare variant, and the scenario-null guard at 0x1800C0DA2 ('tried to switch to a zone-set without a scenario loaded'). The port must reproduce both guards.

verdicts.field: The script impl's tail-call to sub_1802FF07C is unnecessary for the global-write approach
verdicts.claimed: implied - 'the engine clears both globals itself, no cleanup needed', writes alone suffice
verdicts.howIChecked: Raw disassembly shows sub_1800C0D9C does not merely set the two globals: after setting them it tail-calls sub_1802FF07C(ecx = 1) (and the cancel path calls it with 0), and the commit consumer sub_1800C1208 also calls sub_1802FF07C(0) after the switch. I could not establish statically whether that call is merely a notification or whether it gates the main loop from reaching 0x1800BFA89 in some state. Note also sub_1800C12AC (the gate called at the very top of the main update, 0x1800BF94F, whose false result skips the whole pending-work block) reads byte[0x20FF6C1] among a dozen other pending flags - the flag alone does appear sufficient to keep the gate open, which is supportive but not proof. Nothing here can be settled without running the game, which is forbidden.

verdicts.field: prepare_to_switch pending flag is the byte at +0x20FF6C0, index at +0x20FF6CC (they flagged this as a Hex-Rays HIBYTE guess)
verdicts.claimed: guessed +0x20FF6C0, unverified
verdicts.howIChecked: Raw disassembly, exactly the check they said they had not done. sub_1800C0E20: `cmp byte ptr [rip->0x20FF6C0], 0` (0x1800C0E49), `mov byte ptr [rip->0x20FF6C0], 0` (0x1800C0E5D), `mov byte ptr [rip->0x20FF6C0], 1` (0x1800C0E6B), `mov dword ptr [rip->0x20FF6CC], ecx` (0x1800C0E64). Consumer at 0x1800BFA3E: `cmp byte[rip->0x20FF6C0], dil; je ...; mov ecx, dword[rip->0x20FF6CC]; call 0x1800A8DB0`, with the string 'main_prepare_to_switch_zone_set() failed' and a self-clear `mov byte[0x20FF6C0],0; or dword[0x20FF6CC],-1`. Their guess was right; it can be promoted from guess to fact.

verdicts.field: currentZoneSet = halo3odst.dll + 0x8E0B94 (i32, -1 when none)
verdicts.howIChecked: Three code paths, none of them their primary one (they anchored on the current_zone_set script impl; I used the others and verified in raw bytes). (1) sub_1800C0E20 (prepare_to_switch) does `cmp ecx, dword[rip->0x8E0B94]` and on equality emits the string 'tried to prepare to switch to current zone-set %d' - the engine itself calls this global the current zone-set, with the requested zone set index as the comparand. (2) sub_1800A8C34 does the same compare as its first test. (3) sub_1800A8F08 (the commit worker) writes dword[0x8E0B94] = the switched-to index at 0x1800A902E and writes -1 on the failure path at 0x1800A907C; sub_1800A863C resets it to -1 on teardown. I also confirmed the script impl independently: 0x180225830 is `mov ecx,edx; mov edx,[rip->0x8E0B94]; jmp 0x180123B68`, and the name string 'current_zone_set' really is at RVA 0x815DE0 ('switch_zone_set' at 0x815DD0).

verdicts.field: TRAP: HCM's currentBSP for Halo3ODST (0x8E0B90) is NOT the zone set index
verdicts.claimed: 0x8E0B90 is the scenario/map load-state index, must not be reused
verdicts.howIChecked: Their warning is correct and I can sharpen it. Raw disassembly of sub_1800A8348 shows 0x8E0B90 used as a TAG INDEX: `mov eax, dword[rip->0x8E0B90]; movzx ecx, ax; mov eax, dword[rdx + rcx*8 + 4]` where rdx = qword[0xA9F0A8] (the tag table) and the fetched dword is then scaled `lea rax,[r14+rax*4]` with r14 = the magic pointer - i.e. it is the scenario tag's index used to look the scenario tag data up in the cache tag table, after which the code reads the structure-BSP block at +0x1C and iterates 16 BSP bits. My cache parse independently reproduces that exact table format ({u16 groupIdx, u16 salt, u32 addr/4}, address = magic + 4*stored). It is 16-bit-meaningful and is written on scenario load at 0x1800B3B7B. Reusing it as a zone set index would silently produce a plausible wrong number, exactly as they warn.
verdicts.corrected: More precisely than their wording: 0x8E0B90 is the SCENARIO TAG INDEX (a tag handle's low half), not a 'load-state' counter.

verdicts.field: zoneSetCountLocation = i32 at scenario + 0x74
verdicts.claimed: scenario+0x74
verdicts.howIChecked: Cache parse: the dword at scenario+0x74 equals the number of 0x28 elements actually present (25 in h100, 10 in l300, 5 in sc100), each count matching a name run of exactly that length in the string table for h100. Runtime side, in raw bytes rather than decompilation: `cmp ebx,[rax+0x74]; jge -> 'tried to switch to invalid zone-set %d'` at 0x1800C0DC5 and `cmp ecx,[rax+0x74]` at 0x1800C0E3C, with rax = qword[0xA9C9B8], which is byte-identical to HCM's shipped scenarioAddress entry for Halo3ODST (ModuleOffset 0xA9C9B8, deref +0x0).

verdicts.field: maxZoneSets = 0x30 (48), k_maximum_scenario_zone_set_count
verdicts.howIChecked: I deliberately did not re-read their sapien.exe source. I looked for a corroborating runtime constant in halo3odst.dll and found none - the engine bounds-checks only against the per-scenario count at scenario+0x74, exactly as they said. Empirically the largest zone set count I measured in real ODST cache maps is 25 (h100; l300 = 10, sc100 = 5), which is consistent with 48 but proves nothing about the ceiling. Since this value is only a sanity gate in HCM, the safe implementation is to gate on the per-scenario count from the tag block and treat 48 as a soft upper bound, not to rely on it.

verdicts.field: StructureBSPsTagBlock = 0x18 for Halo3ODST (their 'bonus confirmation')
verdicts.howIChecked: Cache parse: the dword at scenario+0x18 is 11 in h100 and the block at +0x1C holds exactly 11 elements at stride 0x6C, each beginning with a genuine 'sbsp' tag reference whose handle low-half indexes a tag whose group table entry is 'sbsp' - and the map contains exactly 11 sbsp tags. Same agreement in l300 (8 and 8) and sc100 (4 and 4). Runtime side: sub_1800A8F08 reads `ecx = dword[scenario+0x18]`, rejects the switch if any bit at or above that count is set in the mask, and sub_1800A8348 iterates bits 0..15 (cmp ebx,0x10) confirming MAXIMUM_STRUCTURE_BSPS = 16.

verdicts.field: switch_zone_set exists as a HaloScript function but HCM has no way to submit script text to an MCC title
verdicts.claimed: exists (name 0x815DD0, impl 0x225804 -> 0xC0D9C); no HCM script injection path
verdicts.howIChecked: String bytes read straight out of the .rdata section of the DLL file: 0x815DD0 = 'switch_zone_set', 0x815DE0 = 'current_zone_set'. Raw disassembly of 0x180225804: `call 0x180124910; movsx ecx, word ptr [rax]; call 0x1800C0D9C` - note the script argument is a SHORT. I also grepped both cases of every identifier (zone_set, ZoneSet, zoneset, 'zone set', ZONE_SET, SwitchZoneSet) across .text/.rdata/.data: 13 hits for 'zone_set', 1 for 'zone set', zero for any CamelCase spelling. On the HCM side, the only script-execution files are HCE-prefixed (HCEConsole, HCEScriptRegistry) and CommandConsoleManager is HCM's own console. Nuance they missed: HaloScriptOutputHookEvent.cpp does instantiate a Halo3ODST implementation - HCM already hooks ODST's HaloScript OUTPUT path, which is read-only but is a real existing foothold if anyone later wants execution.

verdicts.field: Do not call sub_1800A8E60 (main_switch_structure_bsp) from HCM's thread - it uses TLS
verdicts.claimed: reads NtCurrentTeb()->ThreadLocalStoragePointer, engine-thread only
verdicts.howIChecked: Raw disassembly of 0x1800A8E60: `mov edx, dword[rip->0xA8FB1C]; mov rax, qword ptr gs:[0x58]; mov rax,[rax+rdx*8]; mov rbx,[rbx+rax]` with rbx preloaded to 0x40 - a textbook TLS-slot access (gs:[0x58] is the TEB's ThreadLocalStoragePointer on x64, 0xA8FB1C is the TlsIndex). sub_1800A8348 does the same with slot offset 0x368. Their warning stands and is the same trap class as the CER sim-TLS trap.

missedEntirely: The block-address formula. Their prose says 'moduleBase + *(u32*)(scenario+0x78)'. It is actually *(void**)(halo3odst.dll+0x2022AA8) + 4*offset. Their conclusion (reuse HCM's TagBlockReader, which already does magicAddress + (offset<<2) + tagBase=0 for Halo3ODST) is correct, so the port is safe IF it uses TagBlockReader - but any hand-rolled read following their sentence computes garbage. Worth correcting in the handoff because the same sentence also mis-describes 'offset 0 == null block' as a module-relative offset.

string_id_get_string (0x1272C4) can CRASH, it does not just return null. It dereferences *(void**)(module+0x2029340) with no guard and hash_find immediately does `mov rax,[rcx+0x10]` and `div dword ptr [rsi]`. Calling it with no map loaded (the window they themselves identified, since the table is zeroed at 0x1800B3CA5 / 0x18074C853) is an access violation plus a potential divide-by-zero, not a nullptr. The port needs an explicit null/zero-bucket guard, and should only resolve names while a scenario is loaded.

Nobody checked the real data, so nobody noticed that ODST zone sets are ALWAYS named. Across h100 (25), l300 (10) and sc100 (5) every zone set has a non-zero name string_id and not one has the 'internal' bit (0x4) set. The HaloCER '(internal zone set N)' placeholder and the switchable() filter are not just droppable for ODST as they said - they are dead code. Conversely bit0 'begin loading next level' IS set on real zone sets (l300 elements 5 and 9, sc100 element 3), so the GUI can offer a zone set whose selection may start a level transition. That is a user-facing hazard the port should at minimum label in the list.

The pvs index at element+0x04 is bounded by the 'zone set pvs' block at scenario+0x5C (16 entries in h100, and the observed pvs indices are exactly 0..15). If the port ever wants to display or validate it, that is the bound - and it is a cheap extra sanity check that the zone set block was read correctly.

Version fragility is understated. They note the four module offsets are 1.3528-only, but HCM's own XML shows ODST globals in this exact neighbourhood MOVE between builds: the entry at InternalPointerData.xml line ~15951 is halo3odst.dll+0x8E0B98 for 1.3385 and +0x8E0B90 for 1.3528 (an 8-byte shift), while currentBSP stays 0x8E0B90 for 1.3272/1.3385/1.3528. So 0x8E0B94 for currentZoneSet CANNOT be assumed to hold on 1.3385 - it may well be 0x8E0B9C there. The new VersionedEntries must be 1.3528-only (they said this) and someone must redo the four offsets per supported build before shipping to users on older versions.

No firefight/DLC map was checked by either of us. I confirmed the layout on campaign maps h100, l300 and sc100 only. c100.map did not resolve through my pipeline (its structure-BSP run was only 2 elements and the scan did not converge), so it is unverified rather than contradictory. ODST firefight scenario contents remain untested exactly as they admitted.

A practical consequence of the name findings that changes the port's cost estimate: because HCM has no string_id resolver for any H3-era title and the engine call needs guards and is of unproven thread-safety, the GUI may need a fallback that is useful without names - and the ODST switch takes an INDEX, so listing entries as 'zone set N' plus the BSP mask (element+0x0C) and flags is already fully functional. That is a shippable first version that does not block on the resolver.
Halo3ODST.overallReadiness:
Substantially correct and, for the structural half, now independently proven - but NOT ready to implement as written, on two specific points.

Ready to implement (verified by evidence paths independent of theirs - a full parse of the real halo3odst cache maps h100/l300/sc100, raw capstone disassembly bounded by .pdata rather than Hex-Rays, and the H3ODSTEK tag FILE's embedded metadata rather than sapien.exe's definition tables): scenarioZoneSetTagBlock 0x74, stride 0x28, name = u32 string_id at +0x00, the complete ten-dword element layout, flags +0x08 with bit2 = internal, bsp zone flags +0x0C, runtime loaded-BSP mask at module+0x46E261C, count at scenario+0x74, StructureBSPsTagBlock 0x18, currentZoneSet at module+0x8E0B94, the currentBSP 0x8E0B90 trap (which is the scenario TAG INDEX), the pending-switch pair 0x20FF6D0/0x20FF6C1 and its main-loop consumption, the mandatory bounds check, and the TLS warning on sub_1800A8E60. Their prepare-path 'guess' (+0x20FF6C0 / +0x20FF6CC) is now proven in raw disassembly and can be promoted.

Blocked / needs fixing before code is written:
1. NAME RESOLUTION. Their recommendation to call halo3odst.dll+0x1272C4 is based on an incorrect safety characterisation - the function has no null guard and will access-violate (and can divide by zero) if the string_id table at module+0x2029340 is not yet populated. Either add hard guards plus a no-scenario-loaded gate, or ship v1 with index-based labels (the switch takes an index, so names are cosmetic).
2. THE TAG BLOCK FORMULA in their write-up is wrong (magicAddress + 4*offset, not moduleBase + offset). Harmless if the port uses HCM's existing TagBlockReader for Halo3ODST as they recommend; fatal if anyone hand-rolls from their prose.

Still needing RE, in priority order: (a) whether the plain two-global write is sufficient without the engine's own follow-up call to sub_1802FF07C - unprovable statically, and the only remaining behavioural unknown in the switch path; (b) the 1.3385/1.3272 values of all four module offsets, given that HCM's XML already shows ODST globals shifting by 8 between builds in this exact address neighbourhood; (c) maxZoneSets 48 is single-source and uncorroborated - gate on the per-scenario count instead; (d) firefight/DLC scenarios.

verdicts.field: scenarioZoneSetTagBlock = 0x100 (count int32) / 0x104 (encoded block address)
verdicts.claimed: 0x100 — CONFIRMED. int32 count at scenario+0x100, uint32 encoded address at scenario+0x104; tagAddressTable = halo4.dll+0x496A180
verdicts.howIChecked: Two paths, neither of which was theirs (they used Hex-Rays). (1) RAW DISASSEMBLY: I wrote my own PE section mapper + capstone disassembler over halo4.dll on disk and read the actual instruction bytes in five functions: sub_18006252C `44 3b 98 00 01 00 00` = cmp r11d,[rax+0x100]; sub_1800625B8 `3b 88 00 01 00 00`; sub_180045C50 `39 99 00 01 00 00` (count) + `8b 85 04 01 00 00` (enc at +0x104) with the element cursor advancing `add rsi,0x68` per element; sub_18004512C `cmp eax,[rdx+rcx*4+0x100]` / `mov edx,[rdx+rcx*4+0x104]`; sub_1800ED124 `mov r8d,[rax+0x104]`. capstone independently resolved the RIP-relative base to 0x184967A30 and the table to 0x18496A180. (2) REAL CACHE DATA, anchored at the scenario rather than blind-scanned: in m10_crash.map I searched all 567MB for a struct S where dword(S+0x100)==14 and where the single region base C = Zblock - 4*enc simultaneously makes +0xA4, +0xB0, +0x100, +0x304 and +0x328 decode to in-file, same-region, sane targets. Exactly one candidate survives (S=0x1C1E7964): +0xA4 -> a block starting 'psbs' (sbsp tag ref, count 24), +0xB0 -> 'tdds' (sddt tag ref, count 1), +0x100 -> the zone set block at 0x1D03CA20 (count 14), +0x304 -> soft ceilings (count 2), +0x328 -> trigger volumes (count 335). Reproduced end-to-end on m020.map (17 zone sets) and m60_rescue.map (29). Positive control: a deliberately wrong candidate list of 1115 other S values all produce garbage counts (e.g. 3784402008) or out-of-file targets.

verdicts.field: zoneSetStride = 0x1A0
verdicts.claimed: 0x1A0 (416 bytes) — CONFIRMED by three independent sources
verdicts.howIChecked: (1) Raw capstone sweep of the whole .text for `imul r64, r/m64, 0x68` (48/4x 6B /r ib): every zone-set element access is `imul rX, index, 0x68` followed by a [base + rX*4 + disp] operand, i.e. 0x68 dwords = 0x1A0 bytes. Instances at 0x1800ED101, 0x1800ED13A, 0x1800455F7, 0x180045174, and the loop in sub_180045C50 advancing rsi by 0x68 per iteration. (2) THE WALK TEST the brief asked for, anchored at the scenario, not at a pattern scan: from scenario+0x100/0x104 I walked all 14 elements of m10_crash, 17 of m020 and 29 of m60_rescue at 0x1A0 spacing. Every element parses: string_ids strictly contiguous (0x0839..0x0846 / ..0x0849 / ..0x0855 — verified programmatically), audibility index at +0x130 running 0,1,2,...,n-1, hint-previous at +0x12C = -1 everywhere, names all printable. Element[count] (one past the end) is garbage in all three maps (e.g. sid=0x847 name=b'\x07', pvs=983047), which is exactly the boundary behaviour a correct stride predicts. (3) H4EK sapien.exe struct record at file 0x24D5420: {"scenario_zone_set_block", "scenario_zone_set_block", source-path, line 0xCA1, guid, fields=0x1424C8090, 0x1A0, "sizeof(s_scenario_zone_set)"}.

verdicts.field: nameFieldOffset / nameFieldKind: string_id u32 at +0x00 AND char[256] at +0x04
verdicts.claimed: BOTH: string_id_u32 at +0x00 AND char_array_256 at +0x04; prefer +0x04
verdicts.howIChecked: They proved +0x00 from Hex-Rays and +0x04 from cache bytes plus sapien field NAME ordering. I used different routes for both. +0x00: raw disassembly of sub_180045C50 (the script parser's name->index resolver) — `mov ecx, dword ptr [rax + rcx*4]` with ZERO displacement, result passed straight to sub_1800D4F64 (string_id -> char*) and strcmp'd; the loop cursor is rsi += 0x68. So the engine genuinely treats element+0x00 as a string_id. +0x04: I did not eyeball cache bytes, I derived it arithmetically from the H4EK sapien FIELD-TYPE array at VA 0x1424C8090 (0x20-byte records of {u64 type, char* name, u64 def, u64 pad}): type 2 'name^' (string_id, 4 bytes), type 1 'name string*!', type 0x30 'pvs index*!', type 0x0D 'flags', type 0x29 'bsp zone flags', 0x29 'structure design zone flags', 0x29 'runtime bsp zone flags*!', 0x29 'sruntime tructure design zone flags*!', 0x29 'required designer zones{...}', type 0x42 'runtime designer zone flags*!', 0x29 'cinematic zones', 0x30 'hint previous zone set', 0x30 'audibility index*!'. Anchoring that walk on the RUNTIME-PROVEN offsets (0x114 runtime bsp, 0x118 runtime sd, 0x120 8-byte, 0x128 cinematic, 0x130 audibility) forces the type-1 'name string' field to occupy exactly 0x004..0x103 = 256 bytes. Independently, the cache walk shows printable NUL-terminated ASCII at +0x04 zero-filled to +0x104 in all 60 elements across 3 maps. Their advice to read the literal char array and not reimplement the string_id hash lookup is sound; GetDebugString.h does say 'only impl for h2 so far' and there is no Halo4 stringIDDataFields entry in InternalPointerData.xml (I checked: stringIDDataFields has a Halo2 block only).

verdicts.field: bspZoneFlagsTagOffset = 0x10C (authored)
verdicts.claimed: 0x10C — 'bsp zone flags' (uint32, authored), only ever read with TEST (2 sites)
verdicts.howIChecked: Sapien field-type walk (above) places 'bsp zone flags' (type 0x29, 4 bytes) at exactly 0x10C when anchored on the runtime-proven 0x114/0x118/0x120/0x128/0x130. My own capstone sweep found exactly two accesses at +0x10C, both TEST, both 4-byte: 0x180706F84 `test dword [rcx+r8*4+0x10c], r9d` and 0x180707A3E `test dword [rcx+rdx*4+0x10c], eax` — matching their count. Its definition pointer in sapien resolves to 'scenario_structure_bsp_reference_block' with MAXIMUM_STRUCTURE_BSPS_PER_SCENARIO = 0x20, confirming it is a 32-bit mask over the structure-BSP block. Cache: +0x10C == +0x114 in all 60 elements I dumped across 3 maps.

verdicts.field: bspZoneFlagsRuntimeOffset = 0x114 (the one to read/write)
verdicts.claimed: 0x114 — 'runtime bsp zone flags', committed into halo4.dll+0x4967A18
verdicts.howIChecked: Raw capstone, not Hex-Rays: sub_1800ED0EC ends `mov eax, dword ptr [rax + rcx*4 + 0x114]` where rcx = index*0x68 + enc and rax = qword[0x18496A180 + (enc>>28)*8]. sub_180045738 calls it twice, keeps the result in r11d, ORs a second copy with dword[0x4967A68], and passes r11d as r8d to sub_1800457D4. sub_180045584 then writes `mov dword ptr [rip]->0x184967A18, edx` at 0x1800455C2. Fifteen +0x114 read sites in my sweep, all 4-byte MOV, none TEST. Sapien field walk independently lands 'runtime bsp zone flags*!' at 0x114. Semantic cross-check the previous agent did not run: in all three maps the highest set bit index of +0x114 across every element is exactly one less than scenario+0xA4 (m10_crash 23 vs 24; m020 22 vs 23; m60_rescue 26 vs 27) — a mask indexed by the structure-BSP block, as claimed.

verdicts.field: element+0x118 = runtime structure design zone flags
verdicts.claimed: 0x118 — HCM's existing runtimeStructureDesignZoneMask 0x118 is CORRECT
verdicts.howIChecked: Sapien field-type walk puts 'sruntime tructure design zone flags*!' (sic — the engine's own typo) at 0x118. My capstone sweep finds exactly one indexed reader, 0x180044928 `mov eax, dword ptr [rax+rcx*4+0x118]`. HCM's shipping GetActiveStructureDesignTagsImplZoneSet<Halo4> (GetActiveStructureDesignTags.cpp:271, 163-179) already reads scenario ZoneSetTagBlock via tagBlockReader and indexes zoneSetMetaDataStruct at runtimeStructureDesignZoneMask — real-world validation.

verdicts.field: element+0x108 = flags, bit 0x4 = internal zone set
verdicts.claimed: flags at +0x108 {0x1 begin loading next level, 0x2 debug purposes only, 0x4 internal zone set, 0x8 disable sky clearing, 0x10 override sky clear color}
verdicts.howIChecked: Sapien: the 'flags' field record's definition pointer resolves to 'scenario_zone_set_flags_definition' with count 5 and a bit-name array at VA 0x1424C7FD8 that I dumped: bit 0x1 'begin loading next level', 0x2 'debug purposes only', 0x4 'interal zone set*!' (the engine's typo), 0x8 'disable sky clearing', 0x10 'override sky clear color'. Exactly their list. Offset 0x108 falls out of the anchored field-type walk. CAVEAT WORTH SHIPPING: I swept every `imul *,0x68` window in halo4.dll (+/-0x200 bytes, all addressing forms, not just scale-4) and found NO runtime read of element+0x108 at all. So 0x108 is established by the editing kit plus cache values (only 0x0 and 0x10 observed), not by runtime code. Harmless here because the port only uses flags for a cosmetic placeholder.

verdicts.field: element+0x120 is a genuinely 64-bit designer-zone mask
verdicts.claimed: +0x120 uint64 'runtime designer zone flags' (genuinely 64-bit)
verdicts.howIChecked: Capstone operand widths on raw bytes (not Hex-Rays inference): 7 sites at +0x120 with op.size == 8, e.g. 0x1800ED150 `48 8b 84 90 20 01 00 00` = mov rax, qword [rax+rdx*4+0x120] (REX.W). Independently, sapien gives 'runtime designer zone flags*!' type 0x42 — and 0x42 is the only type in the record list that must be 8 bytes wide for the walk to land 'cinematic zones' at the runtime-proven 0x128. Cache agrees: m10_crash elem 4 holds 0x00001007C0001F00, high dword non-zero.

verdicts.field: switchMechanism: write halo4.dll+0x293DEC8 (index) then +0x293DEB4 (flag)
verdicts.claimed: Write two globals; per-tick pump sub_1800607C8 runs `if (byte_18293DEB4) sub_1800626F8();` which calls sub_180045738 and clears both
verdicts.howIChecked: Entirely from raw capstone disassembly of the on-disk PE, plus the one thing they explicitly left unchecked. Producer sub_18006252C: 0x180062592 `c6 05 1b b9 8d 02 01` = mov byte [0x18293DEB4],1 and 0x18006259B `44 89 1d 26 b9 8d 02` = mov dword [0x18293DEC8],r11d. Pump sub_1800607C8: 0x1800609E0 `mov al, byte [0x18293DEB4]` / test al,al / jne -> 0x1800609EA call 0x1800626F8; the adjacent prepare path at 0x1800609D2 tests 0x293DEB3 -> call 0x1800626A0. Consumer sub_1800626F8: 0x18006270A `mov ecx, dword [0x18293DEC8]` -> call 0x180045738, then at 0x180062764 `or dword [0x18293DEC8], 0xffffffff` and 0x180062772 `mov byte [0x18293DEB4], 0` — it does clear both itself. I ALSO CLOSED THE GAP THEY ADMITTED: the pump's entry guard sub_180062828 is a chain of `cmp byte X, 0 / jne return-true`, and 0x1800628D1 reads byte [0x18293DEB4] and returns true if non-zero — so writing our flag opens the gate rather than being ignored by it. The pump has exactly one caller (0x180060C9D, found by scanning every rel8/rel32 branch in .text) and is called unconditionally there. Their mandatory-validation warning is also correct and I strengthened it: sub_1800ED0EC's only guard is `cmp ecx,-1` (0x1800ED0EC) — index -1 is a safe no-op returning 0, but there is NO upper bound and no other negative check, so any index >= count or <= -2 indexes off the block.

verdicts.field: switchMechanismAlternatives (a): 'HCM has no console / script-injection path for any MCC title'
verdicts.claimed: HCM has no console / script-injection path for any MCC title. Grepping HCMInternal hits only HCE* files. Building an MCC script console is a whole separate project.
verdicts.howIChecked: Their grep missed it because none of their search terms ('hs_command', 'script.*inject', 'ConsoleBridge', 'executeScript', 'scriptFunction') matches what the file is actually called. I grepped case-insensitively for a wider set and got CommandConsoleGUI.cpp/.h, CommandConsoleManager.cpp, HaloScriptOutputHookEvent.cpp/.h and GameEngineFunctions on top of the HCE* files. GameEngineFunctions.cpp:47-52 is a working HaloScript path for MCC: `void SendCommand(const char* command) { std::string HScommand = "HS: " + std::string(command); gameEngineDetail->getCommonHandle()->execute_command(HScommand.c_str()); }`. It is GAME-AGNOSTIC — GameEngineFunctionsImpl's constructor ignores the GameState and just resolves GameEngineDetail, and there is no per-game switch anywhere in the file. HaloScriptOutputHookEvent.cpp:379 explicitly instantiates a Halo4 impl, so HCM already reads Halo 4's HaloScript output. CommandConsoleGUI::execute (line 87-111) calls engineCommand->SendCommand for anything not in bannedCommand() (CommandConsoleGUI.cpp:73-84), and that ban list is only game_speed / cheat_deathless_player / game_tick_rate / object_cannot_die+player — 'switch_zone_set' is not banned.
verdicts.corrected: Option (a) IS available for Halo 4: GameEngineFunctions::SendCommand(std::format("switch_zone_set {}", name)). That is the exact shape of the shipped HaloCER implementation (HCESwitchZoneSet.cpp:196 queues the same command string), it runs the engine's own validator sub_18006252C instead of bypassing it, it needs NO new version-locked globals (so it works on 1.3385 and survives future MCC patches), and it does the thread marshalling for you. Its downsides versus the global write: it addresses by name rather than index (fine in practice — names were unique in every map I dumped), and I could not verify at runtime that MCC's execute_command accepts it for Halo 4, because launching the game is forbidden. Recommendation: try SendCommand first and keep the two global writes as the fallback, rather than dismissing (a) outright.

verdicts.field: portNotes #1: 'the tag-block encoding (tagAddressTable[enc>>28] + 4*enc) is already implemented inside TagBlockReaderImplMagic'
verdicts.claimed: The tag-block encoding (tagAddressTable[enc>>28] + 4*enc) is already implemented inside TagBlockReaderImplMagic; do not reimplement it.
verdicts.howIChecked: Read TagBlockReader.cpp. TagBlockReaderImplMagic::read computes `pFirstElement = mOffsetTransformation(*pOffset) + tagBase + magicAddressCached`, where for Halo4 the transformation is `(uintptr_t)in << 2` (TagBlockReader.cpp:99), tagBase is the constant 0x4FFF0000 (InternalPointerData.xml tagBase/Halo4) and magicAddress is halo4.dll+0x28BCD30 deref +0x1E0A8. There is no `enc >> 28` anywhere in the file and no per-region table lookup. It is a single-region affine transform.
verdicts.corrected: The CONCLUSION (use tagBlockReader->read(scenarioAddress + 0x100) rather than hand-rolling) is still right, and tagBlockDataFields/Halo4 is entryCount@0x0 offset@0x4 so passing scenario+0x100 yields count from +0x100 and enc from +0x104 as intended. But the mechanism description is wrong, and it hides a real caveat the port should know: HCM's reader is only correct while every tag block it reads lives in the single region that magicAddress+tagBase was calibrated for. In m10_crash every scenario block I decoded (zone sets, structure BSPs, structure design, soft ceilings, trigger volumes) is region 5 (enc 0x5Exxxxxx), so it holds today — but it is an assumption, not the engine's actual rule.

verdicts.field: StructureDesignTagBlock = 0xB0 (listed by them as a GUESS / NOT ESTABLISHED)
verdicts.claimed: GUESS — do not ship. I did NOT find a runtime read that proves it. If the port needs it, it needs its own pass.
verdicts.howIChecked: Cache data settles it without needing a runtime read. Using the single region base C derived for the m10_crash scenario at S=0x1C1E7964, scenario+0xB0 gives count=1 and scenario+0xB4 gives enc=0x5EEC6316, which decodes to file 0x1D035C58 whose first four bytes are `74 64 64 73` = 'tdds' — the reversed four-CC for 'sddt', the structure design tag group, i.e. the block element begins with a structure-design tag reference exactly as expected. Reproduced on m60_rescue.map (count 4). Positive control in the same decode: scenario+0xA4 lands on 'psbs' ('sbsp'), so the region base is right and the read is not an artefact.

verdicts.field: element+0x128 = cinematic zones, with the evidence 'in every mission +0x128 is 0 for all zone sets EXCEPT the ones whose names begin cin_'
verdicts.claimed: +0x128 is the cinematic-zones mask; in every mission it is 0 for all zone sets EXCEPT ones named cin_*
verdicts.howIChecked: The FIELD IDENTIFICATION is fine — sapien's field walk names it 'cinematic zones' at 0x128 and my sweep finds 9 indexed accesses there including `cmp dword [r8+rdx*4+0x128], 0` at 0x18004560C — but the name-correlation evidence they built the identification on is factually wrong, and I found that by dumping maps they did not (m60_rescue in full, m020 in full). m60_rescue: 'pip_box' has +0x128 = 8, 'trail_c_to_cinematic' = 2, 'outer_deck_to_cin' = 0 despite 'cin' in the name; m020: 'terminus_to_cin_m21' = 4 and '12_field_to_cathedral' = 0. So non-'cin_' zone sets do carry cinematic bits and at least one 'cin'-ish name carries none. Nothing in the port depends on this, but the stated rule should not be repeated as fact.
verdicts.corrected: +0x128 is the cinematic-zones mask (sapien field name + runtime semantics), but it is NOT true that only zone sets named 'cin_*' have bits set. Non-cinematic-named sets such as 'pip_box', 'terminus_to_cin_m21' and 'trail_c_to_cinematic' also carry bits.

verdicts.field: currentZoneSet = halo4.dll+0xE5BB50

verdicts.howIChecked: Rather than counting xrefs, I checked the two places where the value has to be that global for the code to make sense, from raw bytes. missedEntirely: GameEngineFunctions::SendCommand — HCM already has a working HaloScript command path for MCC titles (GameEngineFunctions.cpp:47, `"HS: " + command` through GameEngineDetail::getCommonHandle()->execute_command), it is game-agnostic, HaloScriptOutputHookEvent.cpp:379 already instantiates a Halo4 impl to read the reply, and CommandConsoleGUI already drives it. GetCurrentZoneSet::getCurrentZoneSet() returns uint32_t, not int32_t (GetCurrentZoneSet.cpp). The engine's 'no zone set' sentinel is -1, so the port receives 0xFFFFFFFF. Any `index != currentZoneSet` guard or `<- current` GUI marker that compares signed will misbehave. ZoneSetChangeHookEvent likewise fires eventpp::CallbackList<void(uint32_t)>.

The engine's 'already current' test is NOT just index != currentZoneSet. sub_180045278 returns true only if ALL THREE hold: index == dword[0xE5BB50], the loaded BSP mask dword[0x4967A18] is a superset of element[0x114], AND the 64-bit designer mask qword[0x275D5D0] is a superset of element[0x120]. So re-selecting the current zone set is a LEGITIMATE operation whenever those masks have drifted — which is exactly what happens after HCM's own SwitchBSPSet writes 0x4967A18. A naive `index != currentZoneSet` guard would block the one case where a 're-apply current zone set' button is most useful. The proposed XML comment mandating that check should be softened accordingly.

1.3385.0.0 Halo4 is left unsupported by the proposal in a way that can throw at construction. InternalPointerData.xml already carries Halo4 1.3385 entries for scenarioAddress (0x49679B0, note: different from 1.3528's 0x4967A30), magicAddress (0x28BCCB0), currentZoneSet (0xE5BB50) and ZoneSetChangeFunction (0x455D9). If the new cheat is registered for Halo4 and PointerDataStore cannot resolve pendingZoneSetIndex/pendingZoneSetSwitchFlag on 1.3385, construction fails. Either derive the 1.3385 globals, gate the feature by version, or use SendCommand (which needs no globals at all).

TagBlockReader's actual transform and the two data entries the port silently depends on: magicAddress = halo4.dll+0x28BCD30 deref +0x1E0A8 and tagBase = 0x4FFF0000, combined as (enc<<2) + tagBase + magicAddress. It is single-region, not a tagAddressTable[enc>>28] lookup, and is only correct while every block read lives in the region it was calibrated for (region 5 / enc 0x5Exxxxxx in every campaign scenario block I decoded).

Out-of-range behaviour is worse than 'indexes off the end'. sub_1800ED0EC's ONLY guard is `cmp ecx, -1` (index -1 is a safe no-op returning 0). There is no upper bound and no general negative check, so index <= -2 reads BACKWARDS off the front of the block. Validate 0 <= index < count, not just index < count.

MAXIMUM_STRUCTURE_BSPS_PER_SCENARIO = 0x20 (from the sapien definition the 'bsp zone flags' field points at), matching the runtime guard `if (scenario[0xA4] >= 0x20)` in sub_1800457D4. Relevant if the GUI ever shows which BSPs a zone set pulls in.

The HCM plumbing a new cheat needs, none of which is mentioned: an OptionalCheatEnum entry (HCESwitchZoneSet is at OptionalCheatEnum.h:180 and GetCurrentZoneSet/ZoneSetChangeHookEvent at 102/104), a SettingsStateAndEvents ActionEvent plus a selection setting, a GUIElementEnum value and a GUIElementConstructor case (the HCE one is a hand-written element, not GUIComboEnum), and the per-game GUI layout entry.

GUIHCESwitchZoneSet fires its action on a DETACHED THREAD (mFireEventThreads) purely because HCEConsoleBridge::queue needs to block. Neither the global-write path nor SendCommand needs that, so the detached-thread machinery — and the global mutex in HCESwitchZoneSet.cpp that exists to serve it — should be dropped, not just the switchable()/Entry filter.
