verdicts.howIChecked: Capstone decode of RVA 0xB3548-0xB35A5: 0xB3571 'cmp byte [rip+0x2006138],0' (next 0xB3578) -> 0x20B96B0; 0xB3585/0xB3593 write 0/1 to the same address; 0xB358C 'mov [rip+0x200612A],ecx' (next 0xB3592) -> 0x20B96BC. The drain I observed is at 0xB23A7 'mov byte [rip+0x2007302],dil' -> 0x20B96B0 and 0xB23AE 'or dword [rip+0x2007307],-1' -> 0x20B96BC, i.e. a few bytes from their quoted 0xB2373 - close enough that I treat the identification as right, but the exact drain RVA they quote I did not land on.

verdicts.field: sub_18009C0C0 semantics ('returns true only when the two masks are satisfied')
verdicts.claimed: bool __fastcall(int idx); returns true only when (zoneSet[idx]+0x0C AND loadedBspMask)==zoneSet[idx]+0x0C AND (zoneSet[idx]+0x10 AND designerZoneMask)==zoneSet[idx]+0x10. HCM can reproduce that test purely with reads.
verdicts.corrected: It FIRST does 'cmp ecx, [0x89CADC]' (RVA 0x9C0CA, next 0x9C0D0) and returns false immediately if idx != currentZoneSet. The full predicate is: idx == currentZoneSet AND (element+0x0C & *0x46B70A8) == element+0x0C AND (element+0x10 & *0x46B709C) == element+0x10.
verdicts.howIChecked: Capstone decode of RVA 0x9C0C0-0x9C10B from raw PE bytes. The leading identity check is unmistakable and is why current_zone_set_fully_active (which passes currentZoneSet) works at all. If HCM reimplements 'is zone set N fully loaded' from their description alone, it will report true for a set that merely happens to have its masks covered - a different and wrong answer.

verdicts.field: mask globals: 0x46B70A8 written from zoneSet[i]+0x0C; 0x46B709C derived from +0x10 and +0x14
verdicts.claimed: halo3.dll+0x46B70A8 = loaded structure-BSP mask, written from zoneSet[i]+0x0C; +0x46B709C = active designer-zone mask (derived from +0x10 required and +0x14 forbidden)
verdicts.corrected: Functional roles are right, the provenance is not. In the commit worker r14 = element+8 (proven by the write targets), so: 0x46B709C <- element+0x10 (required designer zones) directly, 0x46B70A0 <- element+0x14, 0x46B70A4 <- r13d, 0x46B7098 <- [rsp+0xA8], and 0x46B70A8 <- ebx, a value computed earlier in the function, NOT element+0x0C.
verdicts.howIChecked: Capstone decode of RVA 0x9C4BC-0x9C4F5 with every RIP displacement resolved from instruction end: 0x9C4BC 'mov r8d,[r14+0xC]', 0x9C4C0 'mov eax,[r14+8]', then 0x9C4CE->0x46B70A8 (ebx), 0x9C4D4->0x46B70A4 (r13d), 0x9C4DB->0x46B709C (eax), 0x9C4E1->0x46B70A0 (r8d), 0x9C4EF->0x46B7098. Since sub_9C0C0 independently proves 0x46B709C is ANDed against element+0x10, eax=[r14+8] must be element+0x10, forcing r14=element+8 - which makes their 'written from +0x0C' claim arithmetically impossible. Harmless for the feature (HCM never writes these) but the note would mislead future RE.

verdicts.field: 'Halo3 has no structure_design (SDDT) system at all'
verdicts.claimed: Halo3 has no structure_design (SDDT) system at all - the scenario tag definition has no StructureDesignTagBlock field
verdicts.corrected: Halo3 absolutely has the structure_design tag group. 'sddt' is group index 132 in the halo3 cache group table (immediately after 'scnr' at 131), and campaign maps ship real sddt tags: 010_jungle 10, 100_citadel 8, 030_outskirts 5. HCM already ships sddtTagDataFields for Halo3 (softCeilingTagBlock 0x10). The TRUE statements are narrower: the Halo3 SCENARIO has no StructureDesignTagBlock field, and the Halo3 zone set element carries no runtime structure-design zone mask.
verdicts.howIChecked: Enumerated the cache group table (183 entries, 16 bytes each, base file 0x144FA5B8, fourcc at +0) and counted tag-instance-table entries whose low-16 group index equals the sddt group index, in three maps. Also grepped HCM's own XML, which contradicts the claim directly.

verdicts.field: zoneSetCountLocation = int32 at scenario+0x58; engine bound-checks against it
verdicts.claimed: cmp ebx,[rax+58h] at RVA 0xB34ED and cmp ecx,[rax+58h] at RVA 0xB3564, rax = qword_180A46A08
verdicts.howIChecked: Capstone on raw PE bytes: 0xB34ED '3B 58 58' = cmp ebx,[rax+0x58]; 0xB3564 '3B 48 58' = cmp ecx,[rax+0x58]; in both functions rax comes from 'mov rax,[rip+...]' resolving to 0xA46A08. IMPORTANT DETAIL FOR THE PORT that the report glosses: both checks are SIGNED and are preceded by 'test reg,reg / js' - the engine rejects negative indices too. HCM's own bound check must be signed, i.e. 0 <= idx < count.

verdicts.field: maxZoneSets = 48 (k_maximum_scenario_zone_set_count)
verdicts.claimed: 48 (0x30), from the H3EK sapien tag_block_definition record
verdicts.howIChecked: I did not use sapien (their path). Independent attempts both came up empty: (a) the literal string 'k_maximum_scenario_zone_set_count' does NOT exist anywhere in halo3.dll, so the runtime carries no such named constant to cross-check; (b) the largest retail count I observed across all 38 halo3 maps is 19 (100_citadel), which is consistent with 48 but proves nothing about the ceiling. This does not matter operationally - as they correctly note and as I confirmed at 0xB34ED/0xB3564, the runtime bound-checks only the live tag block count - so 48 should be treated as a UI sanity constant, not a fact.

verdicts.field: flags at element+0x08, bit 2 (0x4) = internal zone set
verdicts.claimed: flags at +0x08: bit0 'begin loading next level', bit1 'debug purposes only', bit2 'internal zone set'
verdicts.howIChecked: Field OFFSET +0x08 is confirmed by the stride/field walk and by the commit worker (r14=element+8 reads it). The BIT MEANINGS come only from their sapien enum, which I deliberately did not re-read. My independent check: across 138 zone sets in 38 retail Halo3 maps, the +0x08 dword only ever takes the values 0 (131 occurrences) or 1 (7 occurrences). Bit 1 and bit 2 are never set in any shipped map. So 'bit 2 = internal' is untestable from cache data and remains single-source. Practical consequence, which is actually good news for the port: no retail Halo3 zone set is marked internal, so the GUI's internal-set filtering question is moot regardless of which bit it is.

verdicts.field: switch_zone_set exists as a HaloScript function; name string at VA 0x1807F3EA0; arg type 0x1B = 'zone_set' at VA 0x18076E208
verdicts.claimed: Name string at VA 0x1807F3EA0; type 27 name at VA 0x18076E208; table entry base 0x1807E1940, entry size 0x50, +0x38 packed arg info 0x001B0001
verdicts.howIChecked: Raw PE section-table walk (no IDA): 'switch_zone_set\0' is at file 0x7F24A0, .text/.rdata mapped RVA 0x7F3EA0 -> VA 0x1807F3EA0, exactly as claimed; 'zone_set\0' at RVA 0x76E208 -> VA 0x18076E208, exactly as claimed; 'current_zone_set', 'prepare_to_switch_to_zone_set', 'tried to switch to invalid zone-set' (RVA 0x769860) and 'this is not a valid zone set name.' (RVA 0x7CA4B8) all present. The function EXISTS - confirmed. The table-internal details (0x50 entry stride, +0x38 packed arg info, parse-proc slot) I did not re-derive; treat those specific numbers as still single-source, though nothing in the port depends on them.

verdicts.field: HCM has no console/script-injection path for Halo3
verdicts.claimed: HCM has NO console/script-injection path for Halo3 (nothing equivalent to HCEConsoleBridge)
verdicts.howIChecked: Directory listing + case-insensitive grep of the whole HCMInternal tree. Every console/script artifact is HCE-prefixed: HCEConsole.cpp/.h, GUIHCEConsole.h, HCEScriptRegistry.cpp/.h, and the only non-HCE consumers are HCESwitchZoneSet.cpp itself and GUIRequiredServices.cpp. CommandConsoleManager is HCM's own UI console, not a game script queue. So route (a) is indeed not realistic.

verdicts.field: GetDebugString cannot be reused (Halo2-only)
verdicts.claimed: HCM's GetDebugString is Halo2-ONLY
verdicts.howIChecked: Read GetDebugString.h directly. The header carries an explicit comment: 'only impl for h2 so far, because it's not relavent for h1, and third gen (h3+) have a waaaay too complicated system for resolving debug strings'. verdicts.field: HCM has no Halo3 entry for currentZoneSet or ZoneSetChangeFunction, though ZoneSetChangeHookEvent.cpp has a Halo3 case
verdicts.claimed: currentZoneSet exists for HaloReach+Halo4 only; ZoneSetChangeFunction has NO Halo3 entry even though ZoneSetChangeHookEvent.cpp has a Halo3 case
verdicts.howIChecked: Grepped InternalPointerData.xml: the currentZoneSet VersionedEntry contains only Game="HaloReach" and Game="Halo4" blocks; the ZoneSetChangeFunction entry contains zero occurrences of 'Halo3'. Read the factory switch at the bottom of ZoneSetChangeHookEvent.cpp - it constructs ZoneSetChangeHookEventTemplated<Halo3> and <Halo3ODST>. GetCurrentZoneSet.cpp unconditionally resolves nameof(currentZoneSet) for whatever game it is built for. So both services throw at init on Halo3 today. Their proposed midhook site 0x9C4CE is a real instruction ('mov [0x46B70A8],ebx') sitting immediately after the currentZoneSet publish at 0x9C4C7, so the site DESCRIPTION is accurate - but whether it is a safe midhook remains unverified, matching their own flag.

verdicts.field: 1.3385.0.0 offsets extrapolated by -0x1000
verdicts.claimed: HCM's shipped pairs show a consistent -0x1000 shift in halo3.dll data globals; extrapolating gives currentZoneSet 0x89BADC, pending index 0x20B86C0, pending flag 0x20B86B1 - A GUESS
verdicts.howIChecked: Verified the premise from the XML (scenarioAddress 0xA45A08/0xA46A08, magicAddress 0x1FCE4C8/0x1FCF4C8, currentBSPSet 0x46B60A8/0x46B70A8 - all exactly -0x1000), so the pattern is real for .data globals. But only the 1.3528 module exists on this machine, so the extrapolated values cannot be checked and must not ship. Note also that .text RVAs (0xB34C4, 0x108BE0, 0x9C4CE) cannot be extrapolated at all, as they say. Separately, HCM's currentBSPSet entry for Halo3ODST 1.3528 is an EMPTY <Offsets></Offsets> - a pre-existing data hole nobody flagged.

verdicts.field: element tail: 0x24 chocalate mountain override (short block index), 0x26 pad(2)
verdicts.claimed: 0x24 short block index, 0x26 pad
verdicts.howIChecked: Cache data: the dword at element+0x24 is 0x0000FFFF in all 138 zone sets across all 38 maps, i.e. short 0xFFFF (= -1, no override) at +0x24 and short 0 at +0x26. Consistent with the claim and with the stride closing at exactly 0x28. Weak-positive only in the sense that no map ever sets it.

verdicts.field: 'EVERY zone set including internal ones is switchable; the (internal zone set N) placeholder and switchable() filter can be dropped'
verdicts.claimed: Halo3 switching is index-based, so every zone set is switchable and GUIHCESwitchZoneSet's switchable() filter and the '(internal zone set N)' placeholder logic can be dropped
verdicts.howIChecked: Two supports. (a) The switch path is purely index-driven (0x20B96C0 is an int written from ecx; the bound check is against the live count, not against names), so a nameless set is still reachable - this follows directly from the byte-level decode above. (b) No retail Halo3 zone set is flagged internal (138/138 have flags 0 or 1), and all 13 in 010_jungle carry real names. CAVEAT the port must still handle: string_id_get_string returns nullptr on a miss (the 'je 0x180108C30' miss path zeroes the result), so the GUI still needs a fallback label - just index-based ('zone set N'), not internal-based.

missedEntirely: THE NAME-RESOLUTION PLUMBING. They recommend calling halo3.dll+0x108BE0 but never established that HCM has any mechanism to call an arbitrary game function on Halo3. There is no existing 'call into the game' service for this in HCMInternal that they identified; MultilevelPointer resolves addresses, it does not invoke. Someone has to write that (a typed function-pointer wrapper plus a decision about which thread), and it is the single largest unscoped piece of work in the whole port. Until it exists the GUI can only label sets by index.

THE CACHE-FILE PROOF OF THE BLOCK ITSELF. They explicitly say 'I did not locate the zone set block inside the cache FILE'. That omission is exactly why the string_id bug slipped through - they proved the NAMES exist in the string table and assumed the scenario stores the corresponding table index, which it does not. Any future miner on ODST/Reach/H4 must parse the block in the cache, not just the string table. My parser is reusable: index header found by 'sgat' signature, K solved from the group table, tag data addr32<<2-K.

SIGNED BOUND CHECK. The engine's validation is 'test reg,reg / js' followed by a SIGNED 'cmp reg,[scenario+0x58] / jge'. They say 'bound-check the index yourself' without specifying signedness; an unsigned check in HCM would let -1 through to a global the main loop consumes.

INTERACTION BETWEEN THE TWO PENDING SLOTS. prepare_to_switch (0x20B96B0/0x20B96BC) and switch (0x20B96B1/0x20B96C0) are drained within a few instructions of each other in the same main-loop region (0xB23A7, 0xB23AE, 0xB23B5). Nobody examined what happens if HCM stamps the switch globals while a prepare is already pending, or during a level transition. That is the most likely source of a hang or a half-loaded state.

LEVEL-CHANGE INVALIDATION HOOK. They note the scenario pointer moves and the GUI must invalidate, but identified no Halo3 event to hang that on - and the obvious candidate (ZoneSetChangeHookEvent) is itself broken for Halo3 because ZoneSetChangeFunction has no Halo3 XML entry. The port needs either that entry filled or a different invalidation trigger.

NULL-SCENARIO GUARD. Both switch_zone_set and prepare_to_switch begin with 'mov rax,[0xA46A08] / test rax,rax / jz error' - the engine expects the scenario pointer to be null outside a level. HCM's GetScenarioAddress path must reproduce that guard before it reads scenario+0x58, or the feature will fault at the main menu.

Halo3ODST ENTIRELY. Out of scope for them, but HCM's shipped Halo3ODST currentBSPSet for 1.3528.0.0 is an EMPTY <Offsets></Offsets> element - so an ODST port that reuses the BSP machinery is already broken before zone sets are added. Worth fixing in the same pass.

VERIFICATION THAT THE MAIN LOOP AT 0xB2250 RUNS EVERY TICK IN ALL GAME MODES. The whole globals-write recommendation rests on it. Static analysis cannot show this and nobody flagged it as an assumption. If that path is skipped (paused, cinematic, loading), a stamped flag sits pending indefinitely.

WHAT sub_1802D411C(1) DOES. They flagged it as unknown and it remains unknown to me too. I did confirm the shape: the request path tail-calls it with ecx=1 (0xB3522, reached from 0xB3530 'mov cl,1'), and the deferred runner calls it with ecx=0 (0xB389D). So the globals-write route skips exactly one call, the ecx=1 one. If the port glitches on switch, that is the first suspect - and the fix is the direct call to 0xB34C4, which needs a per-tick Halo3 midhook that does not exist.
